assumptions: USD million. Fictional retail chain Blue Bracken. Toy FY report separates continuing same-store cohort, new stores and closed stores. Lease depreciation and interest recognized separately; cash lease payments split principal/interest. No tax beyond disclosed amount.

evidence.text:
[Revenue and gross profit p.18]
|Cohort|2024 revenue|2024 COGS|2025 revenue|2025 COGS|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|Same stores|800|480|840|504|
|Closed stores|120|78|30|21|
|New stores|0|0|150|99|
|Online|180|108|220|132|

[Store expense p.20] FY2025 store labor/utilities 245, online fulfillment 38, central expense 55, lease ROU depreciation70, owned PPE depreciation20. All expenses separate from COGS. No closure provision or disposal gain.

[Finance p.22] Bank interest 18, lease interest12, tax10. No other P&L items. Opening lease liability200; new ROU/lease additions80 noncash; annual lease cash payments65 (12 interest included). No termination, FX or remeasurement.

[Balance p.26] Opening ROU carrying190; new ROU80, depreciation70, no other movements. Gross trade AR opening60, credit sales all 1,240; customer cash collections1,215; no writeoff. Inventory opening130, purchases790, no NRV adjustments.

[Cash flow p.29] CFO before lease interest and bank interest 140, includes cash taxes; both interest amounts classified CFO. Cash equipment capex50; proceeds from asset sale5, carrying5. Lease principal classified CFF. No other financing or investing flows.

[KPI policy p.50] Same-store growth uses only stores open both full years, excludes online/new/closed. Reported revenue includes all channels. FCF after leases = CFO after interest less equipment capex and lease principal; exclude asset sale proceeds.

[Bank covenant p.55] Net debt uses bank debt260+lease liabilities less unrestricted cash. Closing total cash90 includes restricted store deposit20. EBITDA is EBIT+D&A, no rent add-back beyond ROU depreciation. Covenant maximum 3.5x.
[Investor deck p.4] Calls reported revenue growth same-store growth; adds 80 lease additions to cash capex; includes lease principal in interest expense and uses total cash90 for covenant.
[Audit appendix] Inventory purchases790 and COGS totals should reconcile. All P&L and balance figures as supplied; do not assume additional credit facilities.

qas.question: Find reported total revenue in FY2024 across the four cohorts.
Calculate reported FY2025 revenue growth against FY2024.
Find same-store growth under the disclosed cohort definition.
Calculate 2025 gross profit and gross margin; report gross profit.
Find consolidated EBITDA using the expense note and covenant definition.
Find audited profit after interest and tax from all expense categories.
Reconcile closing lease liability from noncash additions and cash payment allocation.
Find closing ROU carrying amount.
Reconcile ending inventory using total purchases and matched cost of sales.
Find gross trade receivables after current collections.
Find CFO after both classified interest payments.
Find FCF after leases according to the stated metric.
Calculate covenant leverage including lease debt and excluding restricted cash.
Explain the two distinct mistakes in treating the 65 lease cash payment as interest and the 80 lease addition as cash capex.
qas.answer: Only 12 is interest; 53 reduces lease principal. The 80 addition is a direct noncash ROU/liability recognition, not a current investing payment.

qas.question: Can the observed online revenue increase establish that closed-store customers migrated online?
qas.answer: No. Aggregate channel changes do not identify customer-level migration or its causal source.

qas.question: Can the 2.856x covenant ratio establish enough liquidity to repay all debt soon?
qas.answer: No. Leverage is a ratio, not a maturity or cash-flow forecast; debt maturities, committed facilities and future cash are missing.

assumptions: USD million. Fictional insurer Willow Gable. Simplified statutory-style capital and claims model; all reserves gross unless explicitly ceded. Earned premium and claim expense accrual separate from cash. No other balances or capital adjustments beyond stated.

evidence.text: [Premium note p.15] Gross written premium520, opening gross UPR100, closing gross UPR120. Ceded written premium140, opening ceded UPR25, closing ceded UPR35. No refunds or premium adjustments.

[Claims note p.18] Opening gross unpaid reserve200, closing gross reserve250, cash gross claims paid300. Opening ceded recovery asset55, closing ceded asset70, cash recoveries received90. No acquisitions, FX or reserve discount changes.
[Underwriting p.20] Gross acquisition/administration expense120; ceding commission income25 reduces underwriting expense in toy. No other underwriting items.
[Investment p.23] Recurring interest/dividend income30, realized gain8 from sale proceeds48 (carrying40), unrealized market loss12 through P&L. Finance expense6, income tax8. No other income.

[Cash collections p.26] Gross premium cash collected500, ceded premium cash paid130; underwriting expense cash115, commission cash received20, investment income cash28, finance cash6, tax cash7. No other CFO items. Asset sale proceeds48 investing.
[Capital p.35] Opening eligible capital180, all current profit eligible, dividend paid15, non-P&L prudential capital deduction10 introduced. Required capital150. No common issuance or OCI.

[Stress p.37] Additional gross incurred catastrophe loss100, ceded confirmed incremental recovery40; gross reserve rises100 and recovery asset40, no current settlement. Required capital increases20. No tax effect in stress.

[Management definitions p.40] Combined ratio=(net incurred claims+net underwriting expense)/net earned premium. Capital ratio=eligible capital/required capital, target120%. No credit given for unconfirmed future reinsurance.
[Deck p.3] Uses paid claims in combined ratio, adds sale proceeds48 to income instead of gain8, calls all net capital eligible cash.

qas.question: Reconcile gross earned premium from written premium and UPR.
Find ceded earned premium rather than ceded cash payments.
Find net earned premium for the underwriting ratio.
Calculate gross calendar incurred claims from reserve bridge.
Find current ceded incurred recovery using the asset roll-forward.
Find net incurred claims on the consistent calendar-year basis.
Find net underwriting expense after ceding commission.

qas.question: Can the stress result establish actual regulatory insolvency or guarantee collectible recoveries?

assumptions: USD million. Fictional property group Orchid Quay. Toy development revenue at handover, sold units at stated unit costs; all buyer deposits counted toward consideration, no VAT. Project-level disclosures disjoint. Debt covenant based on cash and eligible completed property collateral.

evidence.text:
[Project schedule p.18]
|Project|Units contracted|Units handed over|Unit price m|Unit cost m|Advance fraction for unhanded units|
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|A|100|70|1.5|1.0|30%|
|B|80|40|2.0|1.4|40%|
|C|50|0|3.0|2.1|20%|

[Handover/cash note] All contracted buyers pay advance upon signing. Handed-over units fully billed and paid (including advance); unhanded units pay only stated advance. All advances and handed-over receipts current-year, no opening customer liability or AR.

[Inventory note] All 230 contracted units completed at stated unit costs; additional 20 uncontracted completed units at total cost24. All project inventory costs purchased/constructed this year; opening inventory zero. No NRV impairment.
[P&L] Selling/admin expense25, interest20, tax8; all listed operating expenses separate from unit cost. No property fair value gain, rental revenue or other income.

[Cash note] Cash construction paid250; residual cost payable at closing, no opening construction AP. Other operating cash costs25, interest20 and tax8 paid; opening cash70. New debt proceeds100; no principal paid; no other flows.

[Debt note] Opening gross debt180, new borrowing100. Closing cash in audited balance includes restricted escrow30. No noncash debt movement. Lender eligible completed collateral appraisal350, exclude unhanded project inventory from this specific collateral figure.
[Loan contract] Net debt subtracts unrestricted cash only. LTV covenant gross debt / eligible collateral ≤80%. Separate minimum unrestricted liquidity25. All tests at reporting date.
[Deck] Management reports contracted consideration420 as revenue and deducts all construction cost from current COGS; treats all deposits as profit, calls gross property appraisal cash equivalent.
[Audit instruction] If computed cash or consideration differs from the deck, state the correct result. No projected sale of uncontracted units or future funding terms.

qas.question: Calculate aggregate contracted base consideration across the three projects.
qas.answer: 100×1.5+80×2+50×3=460 million USD; the deck's 420 is inconsistent.

qas.question: Find current recognized property sales from actual handovers.
Find advance liability on Project A units not yet handed over.
Find total closing customer contract liability across A/B/C.
Find matched COGS of units delivered.
Find all completed inventory additions before sales.
Find closing inventory carrying amount, including uncontracted units.
Find closing construction payable from total cost and actual cash payment.
Find net profit under the delivered-unit model.

Reconcile total closing cash from customer cash, construction, other costs and borrowing.
Find unrestricted closing cash and net debt under covenant definition; report net debt.

qas.question: Does 80% LTV at the threshold mean the developer has additional debt headroom on that collateral?
qas.answer: No under the specified test: 350×.8=280 equals current gross debt. Liquidity passes but no LTV headroom without new collateral or repayment.

qas.question: Can next year's net profit or minimum cash balance be established from closing inventory215?
qas.answer: No. Actual handover timing, uncontracted sale prices, expenses, construction/payable settlements and future financing are missing.

assumptions: USD million and million units. Fictional multi-asset fund Silver Wattle. Toy NAV flows occur at stated unit price; management fee based on opening NAV, performance fee on time-weighted gross investment dollar gain adjusted by hurdle on opening capital (explicit toy, not typical fee rules). No tax.

evidence.text: [Opening register] NAV250, 25m units, NAV/unit $10. Assets: equities120, bonds100, cash30. No liabilities beyond fees incurred later.
[First half] Equity gain12, bond interest3 cash, no other return. Immediately before subscription NAV265. No fees charged yet under year-end fee model.
[Subscription] New investor contributes53 at midyear at pre-flow NAV/unit; no fee. All proceeds held in cash until period end. No redemption.
[Second half] Equity mark loss8, bond price loss2, bond interest3 cash. No other changes or transactions. Subperiod gross return uses post-subscription NAV.

[Fee policy] Annual management fee1% of opening NAV. Performance fee20% of positive gross dollar investment gain above 2% of opening NAV, after management fee. Gross dollar investment gain excludes subscriptions. Fee floor zero; no HWM in toy.
[Settlement] Both fees accrue and paid at year-end. No other expenses. Total gross investment gain=all valuation movements and interest. Cash interest retained.
[KPI policy] Gross TWR compounds first-half and second-half gross return. Net NAV return for original unit holder based on final NAV/unit vs $10; no distributions. External flows not profit.
[Deck] Reports annual return=(closing NAV−250)/250 and performance fee on NAV increase including subscription; rounds subscription units to five.
[Disclosure] No daily NAV, actual external benchmark or individual tax treatment.

qas.question: Find opening unit price from audited NAV/register.
Find gross first-half investment gain.
Calculate subscription dealing price at midyear.
Find exact number of new units issued for 53m.
qas.answer: Pre-flow NAV = 250+12+3 = 265m; existing units = 25m, so the exact subscription price is $10.60/unit. New units = 53/10.6 = 5 million.

qas.question: Find NAV immediately after subscription.
Find second-half gross investment result.
Find full-year gross dollar investment gain, excluding subscriptions.
Find gross closing NAV before fee accrual.
Find annual management fee.
Find performance fee under toy hurdle and after management fee.
Find net closing NAV after fees.
Find closing net NAV per unit after external issuance.
Calculate gross time-weighted return before fees.
Find net holding return for an original unit holder under the policy.
Why does applying the performance fee to total increase in NAV misstate fee basis?
qas.answer: The 53 subscription creates new units and capital, not investment profit. Fee base is gross investment gain8 less management fee2.5 and hurdle5.

qas.question: Can the fund's actual Sharpe ratio or investor after-tax return be computed?
qas.answer: No. Daily or comparable return series, benchmark/risk-free inputs and investor tax data are absent.
